sentences.en: And welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，这是一个探讨我们在二十岁时遇到的一些重大生活变化与转型及其对我们心理学意义的播客。

sentences.en: Hello everybody, welcome back to the show, welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到本节目，欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here for another episode.

sentences.en: Today, we're going to discuss something that I think happens quite a bit in our 20s, but never really receives the same acknowledgement or attention that it deserves.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讨论一件我认为在我们二十岁时经常发生，却从未真正得到应有的认可或关注的事情。

sentences.en: We hear a lot about breakups, about romantic relationships that end, but what about our platonic relationships?
sentences.zh: 我们听过很多关于分手、关于浪漫关系结束的事情，但我们的柏拉图式关系呢？

sentences.en: What about our friendships?
sentences.zh: 我们的友谊呢？

sentences.en: What I really want to explore today is that experience of outgrowing your friends, of outgrowing relationships and why it's really natural and really normal
sentences.zh: 我今天真正想探讨的是超越朋友、超越关系的经历，以及为什么发现童年、高中或大学时最好的朋友不再是同一个人是一件非常自然、非常正常的事情，

sentences.en: and maybe even a step beyond that, even beneficial in some ways to find that your childhood, high school or university best friends are no longer the same people,
sentences.zh: 甚至可以说是超越这一步、在某些方面甚至是有益的发现，

sentences.en: you're no longer the same person and noticing when it is time to move on and dealing with that experience.
sentences.zh: 而你也不再是同一个人，并注意到什么时候该向前看以及如何处理这种经历。

sentences.en: I think that our idea of friendship growing up and in our late teens, even early 20s, is often quite unrealistic and highly romanticised.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们成长过程中以及在十几岁后期甚至二十岁初时对友谊的看法往往非常不切实际且高度浪漫化。

sentences.en: We see friendships, unlike our romantic relationships, as these everlasting relationships that are only disrupted by huge falling outs or massive events
sentences.zh: 我们认为友谊与浪漫关系不同，是那种只有在发生巨大决裂或重大事件时才会被打破的永恒关系，

sentences.en: that either last forever or come to an end in an instant.
sentences.zh: 要么永远持续下去，要么瞬间结束。

sentences.en: But as we enter our 20s, we can see that friendships are a lot more nuanced and not always black and white.
sentences.zh: 但当我们进入二十岁时，我们会发现友谊要微妙得多，并非总是非黑即白。

sentences.en: Like any relationship, they can be emotionally complex and confusing, but drifting away from a friend isn't a bad thing, it's actually an entirely natural part of growing up
sentences.zh: 就像任何关系一样，它们可能在情感上很复杂且令人困惑，但与朋友渐行渐远并不是一件坏事，这实际上是成长过程中完全自然的一部分，

sentences.en: and growing into yourself.
sentences.zh: 也是成长为你自己的过程。

sentences.en: You don't have to feel ashamed or like you owe anyone an explanation, it's actually fairly common and I really want to normalise this experience.
sentences.zh: 你不必感到羞耻，也不觉得自己欠任何人一个解释，这其实相当普遍，我真的很想让这种经历变得正常化。

sentences.en: I think another lesson we are bound to learn in our 20s is that when it comes to friendships, quality over quantity is always the way.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在二十岁时注定要学到的另一个教训是，当谈到友谊时，重质不重量永远是王道。

sentences.en: I think when I was in my early years of university, I had this tendency and need to be friends with everyone I met and maintain those relationships,
sentences.zh: 我想当我在大学初期的几年里，我有这种倾向和需求，想和遇到的每一个人做朋友并维持这些关系，

sentences.en: even when we both realised we were incompatible.
sentences.zh: 即使我们两个人都意识到我们并不合适。

sentences.en: It was exhausting to try and have these special moments, deep conversations and vulnerability with everyone, even people who I knew would probably never get me.
sentences.zh: 试图和每个人都有这些特殊的时刻、深度的对话和敞开心扉，甚至是和那些我深知可能永远无法理解我的人在一起，这让我筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: But when I began to unpack the root cause of that habit, that really I was just terrified of being alone and not constantly being surrounded by people,
sentences.zh: 但当我开始剖析那个习惯的根本原因时，发现我其实只是害怕孤独，害怕不被人群时刻包围，

sentences.en: I was able, I think, to become a lot more selective and really pour my love and appreciation and time into the people and into the friendships that meant the most to me.
sentences.zh: 我想我变得更有选择性了，能够把我的爱、感激和时间真正倾注在那些对我意义最重大的人和友谊上。

sentences.en: The result of this was kind of a period of about 12 months or so where I found that my social circle just slowly began to shrink
sentences.zh: 这样做的结果是，大约有12个月左右的时间，我发现我的社交圈开始慢慢缩小，

sentences.en: and I naturally drifted away from a lot of these people that I was trying so hard to stay friends with.
sentences.zh: 我自然而然地和许多我曾经拼命想要维持友谊的人渐行渐远。

sentences.en: And that was really scary.
sentences.zh: 这真的很吓人。

sentences.en: I felt like I'd abandoned these friends and they'd abandoned me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我抛弃了这些朋友，而他们也抛弃了我。

sentences.en: But as time goes on, I think it gives us the hindsight and the wisdom to realise that sometimes friendships need to fizzle and end for you to find new versions of yourself
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，我认为这赋予了我们事后的诸葛亮般的智慧，让我们意识到有时候友谊需要消亡和结束，你才能找到新版本的自己，

sentences.en: and for you to find new people who will match your energy and your identity.
sentences.zh: 并且让你找到能够与你的能量和身份相匹配的新人。

sentences.en: So today I want to break down why we outgrow our friendships, especially during this decade of huge personal growth and transformation when we can recognise that a friendship
sentences.zh: 所以今天我想剖析一下为什么我们会与朋友渐行渐远，尤其是在这个充满巨大个人成长和转变的十年里，当我们意识到一段友谊

sentences.en: is perhaps feeling a little bit stale or unfulfilling.
sentences.zh: 也许让人觉得有点乏味或无法满足时。

sentences.en: The research, the psychology behind this that concludes that this is actually a healthy experience and one that we should come to value and accept
sentences.zh: 研究和背后的心理学结论表明，这其实是一种健康的经历，是我们应该开始重视和接受的经历，

sentences.en: but also discussing some of those harder parts of this experience.
sentences.zh: 但同时也要讨论这种经历中一些比较艰难的部分。

sentences.en: You know, how to end things in a good place, how to process sometimes even the grief for what used to be.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如何体面地结束一段关系，如何有时甚至去消化对过去那些日子的悲伤。

sentences.en: And finally, the value of solitude and how to feel comfortable with being alone as we outgrow certain people in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 最后，独处的重要性以及在我们二十岁时超越某些人之后，如何对独处感到舒适。

sentences.en: I think there's a pretty general fear that as we age, we're going to become more isolated and these large networks will disappear.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一种普遍的恐惧，即随着我们年龄的增长，我们会变得更加孤立，这些庞大的社交网络将会消失。

sentences.en: So what we do is we maintain relationships with people out of habit and out of fear, even when we know that we've outgrown each other.
sentences.zh: 所以我们所做的就是出于习惯和恐惧去维持与人们的关系，即使我们明知彼此已经渐行渐远。

sentences.en: Firstly, I don't think that that's necessarily accurate that, you know, we'll never have more friends than we have in our 20s but that fear also highlights an important skill
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为这不一定准确，你知道的，我们以后永远不会拥有比二十岁时更多的朋友，但这种恐惧也突显了一项重要技能，

sentences.en: that we need to prioritise during this decade which is the ability to enjoy time spent alone and in our own company and learn to walk away from the relationships
sentences.zh: 我们需要在这十年里优先培养这项技能，那就是享受独处和陪伴自己的能力，并学会远离那些

sentences.en: that don't serve us and let other people do the same.
sentences.zh: 不再适合我们的关系，并让其他人也这样做。

sentences.en: So let's get into it and discuss the nuances and explanations behind why we outgrow our friendships.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们切入正题，讨论我们为什么会与朋友渐行渐远背后的微妙之处和解释。

sentences.en: I think it goes without saying that friendships are some of the most valuable relationships that we will experience in life and good friends, they are even more valuable.
sentences.zh: 不言而喻，友谊是我们人生中经历过最有价值的关系之一，而好朋友则更有价值。

sentences.en: They improve our mental and physical health.
sentences.zh: 它们改善了我们的身心健康。

sentences.en: You know, a 2017 study found that close friendships are a huge predictor of improved mental health, cognitive functioning and even reduced anxiety and stress levels.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，2017年的一项研究发现，亲密的友谊是改善心理健康、认知功能甚至降低焦虑和压力水平的重要预测指标。

sentences.en: You know, friendship literally has a psychological capacity to change our bodies and to change our brains for the better.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，友谊确实具有改变我们的身体和大脑向更好方向发展的心理潜能。

sentences.en: But friendship is not always black and white and it's very natural to find that the older we get, the more of our friendships we tend to outgrow.
sentences.zh: 但友谊并不总是非黑即白的，而且随着年龄的增长，我们会发现越来越多的友谊被我们抛在身后，这是非常自然的。

sentences.en: There are many reasons why we find that a friendship that used to be the perfect fit full of special moments and compatibility has suddenly changed and it's no longer right for us
sentences.zh: 有很多原因让我们发现，一段曾经完美契合、充满特殊时刻和默契的友谊突然变了，它不再适合我们

sentences.en: in our current period of life.
sentences.zh: 当前的人生阶段。

sentences.en: Often it's a slow realization brought on by distance or change in circumstances where we gradually come to realize that what once was is no longer and we may be holding on
sentences.zh: 通常这是一种由距离或环境变化带来的缓慢领悟，我们渐渐意识到曾经的已不复存在，我们可能只是为了怀旧，

sentences.en: But the thing that makes outgrowing friendships so natural and normal is that it aligns with those changes and moments where we are outgrowing old versions of ourselves
sentences.zh: 但让超越友谊变得如此自然和正常的原因是，它与那些我们超越旧版本自己的变化和时刻相一致，

sentences.en: and with that the relationships that were part of that former identity as we grow up as we age we will inevitably shift and change we will take on new hobbies and attitudes beliefs

sentences.en: I think that's one of the things that keeps life from being boring is knowing that we are constantly shifting into a deeper different but hopefully more mature version of ourselves
sentences.zh: 我认为正是这一点让生活免于乏味，那就是知道我们一直在转变成更深沉、不同但希望更成熟的自己，

sentences.en: and that we can reinvent ourselves and try new things at any time especially in our 20s when this is not only permissible but highly encouraged by our society.

sentences.en: isn't necessarily over it may have faded a bit and lost some of that deepness and connection you formerly had and that it's okay it's a sign of growth a sign of development
